1982: Roll gates rising in relay, coffee carts docking on corners. Runners owning the bridges, the day clocking in with wet hair
1983: The first coffee wave visible as one golden tide across a million counters. School buses surfacing, the express platforms filling like locks in a canal
1984: Full rush, the great choreography of eight million entrances, revolving doors spinning like turbines. The grid at capacity with two collisions and one apology
1985: Elevators docking, the second coffee, markets opening with a bell somebody still gets to ring. Delivery bikes threading the settled grid
1986: Museums unlocking to school trips, laundromats in first spin. Retirees claiming benches with newspapers, the day's second shift of intentions
1987: Prep kitchens at full chop, playgrounds at full scream. The early lunch scouts already moving, the morning cashing out its promises
1988: Food cart lines like sundial shadows, church bells and jackhammers splitting the hour. Every plaza blooming with sandwiches, the sun directly invoiced
1989: The long lunch and the eaten desk, chess tables at full clock. The first hooky matinee ticket sold to someone deserving
1990: The naptime armistice, strollers docked in cafe shade, offices at half hum. The light beginning its long lean toward the river
1991: School doors detonating borough wide, bodega candy futures spiking. Crossing guards conducting the day's great migration home
1992: The shift change hour, cabs going dark mid avenue, family meal at the back tables. Homework spreading across bodega counters, the day trading crews
1993: The reverse tide, platforms breathing in, one million loosened ties. The first legitimate beer sweating somewhere with its shoes off
1994: Golden hour hitting the avenues lengthwise, stoops filling, ovens lighting. The day's armor coming off block by block
1995: Dinner steam in every airshaft, curtain calls for the sunset on every roof. The night writing its guest list
1996: Curtains rising in forty theaters, first dates mid gamble, kitchens at full sail. A million windows switching on like an orchestra tuning
1997: Second bottles and homework surrendered, dog walkers on last patrol. The skyline fully lit and slightly overdressed, everything still possible
1998: Kitchens breaking down as bars build up, trains carrying perfume one way and flour the other. The night's first regret filed, the second round called
1999: Encores and closing kitchens, rooftops trading the skyline's gossip. Last trains promised and believed, the day writing its final drafts
2000: The hinge of everything, yesterday and tomorrow shaking hands on every corner. One baker starting as one dancer finishes, the eye flowers all open at once
2001: Resolution runners and radiator clank, snow turning gray gracefully. Soup steam on every window, the year still folded like new shirts
2002: The shortest month's longest weeks, roses on trains and slush moats at corners. One absurdly warm day, cruelly rescinded
2003: Wind auditioning for april, green bagels and false springs. Coats opened then regretted, the year's first stoop sitters testing the light
2004: Cherry petals in the gutters like confetti after a parade, umbrellas ambushed twice daily. The parks rehearsing their comeback in public
2005: Stoops in session and windows finally up, the first hydrant negotiation. Lilacs arm wrestling exhaust and winning by a nose
2006: Last days of school and first days of everything, pride flags and pool keys. The evening stretching itself like a cat until nine
2007: Hydrants open and rooftops claimed, the ice cream truck's empire at zenith. Thunderstorms clearing the stage nightly for fireflies
2008: Half the block upstate and the other half at peace, alternate side suspended like a blessing. Tar beach at full occupancy, the pace finally honest
2009: New sneakers and sharpened intentions, the light turning scholarly. One week of perfect weather issued as apology, the year's second january
2010: Stoops sprouting pumpkins and skeletons, the perfect two weeks cashed in. Marathoners tapering, every tree running its own fire sale
2011: Parade balloons sleeping under nets, ovens drafted borough wide. The early dusk forgiven for one week of gratitude, leaves finishing their run
2012: Tree lots perfuming the corners, windows dueling in lights. The year sprinting and strolling at once, every tradition reporting for duty
2013: January's full moon over the frozen reservoir, coyote song from the north woods answered by sirens. The running path silvered, winter's first full confession
2014: February's moon lighting a blizzard's aftermath, plow mountains glowing like alps at the curbs. One cross country skier owning fifth avenue
2015: March's moon over softening park soil, robins working the night shift. The first earthworms surfacing to a kid's flashlight rescue patrol
2016: April's moon rising behind the flowering trees, petals falling silver in the light. One rooftop proposal timed to the minute of moonrise
